newsitem.title: UK: IBCA likely to up UK building societies' sub debt.
newsitem.headline: IBCA likely to up UK building societies' sub debt.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Thursday it is likely to upgrade the dated, subordinated debt of those British building societies converting to banks, when the conversions take place.
IBCA said the ratings were likely to be raised to one notch below senior debt from two notches below.
The building societies concerned, which are all intending to become banks in mid-1997, are Alliance & Liecester, Halifax, Northern Rock and Woolwich.

"The reason for the lower rating of building society subordinated debt is the deeper subordination than bank subordinated debt," IBCA said in a statement. "In a winding up, bank subordinated debt ranks before preference and ordinary shares. Building society subordinated debt ranks after retail share accounts, typically 70 percent or more of the balance sheet, and may rank last if there are no permanent interest bearing shares."

"However, the upgrade is unlikely to apply to undated subordinated debt which, because it is closer in character to equity and ranks after dated subordinated debt, will remain two notches below senior debt," the rating agency said.
